claims.promise: In Original mode the item's own pixels are never regenerated: the cut-out is composited over a new background and a test proves the interior bytes are identical to the source.

comparison.limitation: Renders each slide through a generative model, refunds only technical failures, and its own page documents a hyphenation error in the drawn text.

evidence.finding: Nightjar separates realism from fidelity and names the conventional cut-out composite as the pipeline that retains the captured product pixels; WB lists a neural photo with distorted characters among errors that lower a card's rating.

proof.assertion: Running this unit test composes an Original-mode cut-out at unit scale and verifies every output pixel equals the source pixel.

claims.promise: A result that fails, times out, or is rejected by the fidelity guard costs the user no credits, while competitors charge for a frame the user dislikes.

comparison.limitation: An unsuccessful frame by the user's taste debits a credit just like a successful one; only technically failed generations are refunded.

evidence.finding: WildCard's own page states an unsuccessful frame debits a credit like a successful one and only technical failures are refunded automatically.

proof.assertion: A guard-rejected cut-out projects a Released credit outcome and asks the wallet to refresh, while a successful job projects no refund: the client reads the non-charge off the ledger (reserved == released, charged == 0), so a result the seller dislikes costs nothing. JobMoneyPresentationTest.driftingGuardResultIsPresentedAsReleasedOnlyWhenTheServerReportsFullRelease proves the release is shown only when the server itself reports the full release, and ApiClientTest asserts status.notCharged on the terminal payload.

claims.promise: One tap recognises the kind of item and builds a card with a background and shadow that fit that category, in the marketplace's own mode.

comparison.limitation: Generated composition is a test feature behind the Jam tariff, returns two variants per press and each press spends the studio limit.

evidence.finding: WB help of 2026-03-02 says generate composition works in test mode, needs the Jam subscription from 22 990 RUB per 30 days, and each press reduces the studio limit by 1.

proof.assertion: The live GeneratedSceneRoute launches AutoCardRecognitionViewModel for the selected photo; recognizePhotoForAutoCard calls ApiClient.recognizePhoto with a 1024px-long-side JPEG and maps category, attributes and scaleHint into AutoCardFlowState. AutoCardEngine uses that category's generated recipe, shadow and fill settings plus observed attributes and scale to build the prompt submitted by StudioViewModel as GENERATED_SCENE. Sellers can correct the category, attributes and scene; explicitly supplied categories skip recognition. Supplied marketplace rules constrain the prompt and original-only returns the source. Offline, failed, malformed and zero-confidence recognition require seller selection, never an invented category. AutoCardGeneratedRecognitionTest exercises the API-to-generated-job payload and failure/manual branches; AutoCardFlowTest and AutoCardCatalogDifferentiationTest retain local-recipe coverage. No local gradient is presented as generated AI output.

claims.promise: Every image is checked against the stated rules of the chosen marketplace with a sourced, dated preset, and one button fixes what can be fixed.

comparison.limitation: A general editor with marketplace templates and no per-marketplace rule check with a source and a verification date.

evidence.finding: Marketplace rules differ per platform and drift: WB's own help pages state two different minimum sizes (700x900 and 700x933) and Vinted forbids image editing altogether.

proof.assertion: The linter panel rendered inside ExportScreen calls MarketplaceLinterAction.checkAndRepair from one button, which lints every pack against the dated preset and applies MarketplaceLinterRepair to each finding that editing can satisfy; a finding editing cannot satisfy is reported instead of being passed. MarketplaceLinterRepairTest.downscaleFixRepairsImageAndRelintsWithoutTheFinding and MarketplaceLinterRepairTest.findingThatCannotBeEditedIsNeverReportedAsFixed cover both outcomes.

claims.promise: A look saved from one card applies to a whole batch in one action, resumes after a restart, and retries only the items that failed.

comparison.limitation: Described as one image at a time with limited batch.

evidence.finding: Photoroom's batch editor handles up to 50 images and Pixelcut is described as one image at a time with limited batch.

proof.assertion: BatchViewModel applies one saved look to every selected source in start(), resumes an interrupted batch in resume() and re-queues only the items whose state is FAILED in retryFailed(); the same artifact carries the bulk-selection API toggleSelection/selectAll the bulk family is read from.

claims.promise: One action exports a pack per marketplace with the right sizes, formats and SKU file names, through the share sheet, the gallery or a ZIP, with a manifest of any rule the seller overrode.

comparison.limitation: One image per run, a single marketplace and no cross-marketplace transfer.

evidence.finding: A third-party blog dated 2026-09-22 lists the Ozon editor's gaps as one image per run, a single marketplace and no cross-marketplace transfer.

proof.assertion: ExportDelivery provides share-sheet, gallery and ZIP destinations; export tests verify marketplace packs, SKU filenames, preset dimensions and override manifests.

claims.promise: An infographic series is set in one saved style with the same background on every slide and text the seller chose, typeset on the device and checked against the marketplace's prohibited-text list before it renders.

comparison.limitation: Regenerates the background for every slide, so the same background across a series will not exist, and renders text through the generative model.

evidence.finding: WildCard's own page states the same background across a series will not exist and that it has no change-only-the-background command; WB's help lists prices, contacts, evaluative words and calls to action as prohibited slide text.

proof.assertion: renderSeries checks every slide against marketplace text rules before producing layouts that reuse the saved background and preserve seller-provided text.

claims.promise: Many photos come in at once from the system photo picker with no storage permission, with duplicates flagged and big batches imported in chunks.

evidence.finding: A seller works on many items per session; the Photo Picker needs no runtime permission, which follows from the Android Photo Picker contract and keeps the permission list short.

proof.assertion: The system photo picker accepts multiple photos in one selection, up to the screen's five-photo limit.

claims.narrowedTo: The system picker imports up to five selected photos sequentially and reports per-photo failures.
claims.lostCoverage: Duplicate selections are not flagged, and the screen does not accumulate larger batches across picker chunks.

claims.promise: A camera coach with a level, a framing overlay for the chosen marketplace and a shot list per item category helps the seller take a usable photo before editing starts, working without a network.

evidence.finding: Marketplace rules constrain the source photo (aspect, fill, main-photo content), so guidance at capture time removes fixes later; no competitor in the compared set is documented as offering capture guidance.

proof.assertion: CoachRoute combines the photo picker and camera capture with a marketplace framing overlay, level indicator and category shot list; these local capture flows work without network calls.

claims.promise: Photos are grouped into items with SKU patterns, and a ruler, label or scale hint in a photo is read and confirmed by the seller to size the item correctly in the card.

evidence.finding: Sellers manage multiple photos per SKU across marketplaces; the capability is a recognition read whose accuracy spike S3 measures before it is promised in the UI.

proof.assertion: Running this test groups product photos according to the seller's SKU pattern.

claims.narrowedTo: Photos can be grouped into seller-SKU items, with reference photos kept out of exports.
claims.lostCoverage: The app does not read a ruler, label or scale value from photos or ask the seller to confirm a measured item size.

claims.promise: Titles, descriptions and key attributes are written in the language and within the length limits of the chosen marketplace, in six languages, and can be copied or shared.

comparison.limitation: Sells an SEO pack as a separate paid unit inside a chat bot, not tied to the photo set in a project.

evidence.finding: WildCard's own page prices an SEO pack at 1 credit as a separate unit.

proof.assertion: The listing screen composes marketplace-limited text in the six supported languages and exposes copy and share actions.

claims.promise: Past projects are found again by SKU, category, marketplace or text, with bulk re-export and bulk marketplace change.

evidence.finding: A seller reuses cards across marketplaces and seasons, and the research behind the depth rule ranks find-it-again among the extras users ask for.

proof.assertion: LibraryViewModel filters past projects by the searchQuery text, category, marketplace and updated-date range, and acts on many at once through reExportSelected() and changeMarketplaceForSelected(); the searchQuery token the find family is read from lives in this same artifact.

claims.promise: A notification tells the seller when a long batch has finished, so the phone can be put away while it works.

evidence.finding: Server operations take on the order of tens of seconds each (WB's own generator returns in about a minute), so a batch outlasts a seller's attention.

proof.assertion: BatchNotifier creates its notification channel and posts a completion notification with completed and failed item counts.

claims.promise: Saved looks survive a phone change through backup rules, and an interrupted batch resumes without redoing finished items; the wallet is deliberately excluded from cloud backup.

evidence.finding: Looks are the seller's reusable work product, and a wallet in a backup would let credits be copied between devices.

proof.assertion: The manifest enables the extraction rules that include saved Looks in backup; the Room-backed batch queue and restart test preserve and resume unfinished work without repeating completed items.

claims.promise: Labelled, fidelity-guarded studio operations (relight, expand, erase, upscale, recolour, garment ghost mannequin and virtual model) are available beside Original mode, each with its cost shown first and disabled where a marketplace forbids editing.

comparison.limitation: Offers virtual model, ghost mannequin and recolour as a general editor without a guard that compares the result against the source item.

evidence.finding: An independent comparison dated 2026-04-08 lists Photoroom's virtual model, ghost mannequin, staging, recolour and flat lay among its features, with no stated fidelity check.

proof.assertion: The catalog names enhanced studio operations, calculates their credit costs and exposes marketplace, fidelity and configuration gates that can mark them unavailable.

claims.narrowedTo: The studio catalog exposes named, priced enhanced-operation offers and reports their marketplace and fidelity availability gates.
claims.lostCoverage: The named enhancement operations are not generally available or guaranteed to execute; they remain disabled unless their server route and measured-fidelity configuration are enabled.
